classification_reason: A useful noun for distinctive personal habits and unexpected system behavior, including technical discussion.

senses.definition: An unusual habit or characteristic that makes a person distinctive.
senses.example: One of her quirks is that she organizes every file by color.

synonyms.note: more formal and often emphasizes individuality
broader and may describe anything unusual

senses.definition: An unusual and sometimes inconvenient feature of a system, rule, or situation.
senses.example: Because of a quirk in the API, empty arrays are returned as null.

synonyms.note: more formal and less likely to suggest inconvenience
usually an irregular result rather than an established feature

classification_reason: A recognizable concept in psychology, entertainment, and fiction, but a specialized noun with limited productive value.

senses.definition: A state of highly focused attention in which a person is more responsive to suggestions.
senses.example: She described feeling deeply relaxed under hypnosis.
senses.usage_note: Uncountable; common patterns include under hypnosis and use hypnosis.

classification_reason: A useful verb for dishonest manipulation and equipment setup, with common technical noun senses; the submitted form was normalized from rigged to rig.

senses.definition: To control or arrange a result dishonestly so that someone gains an unfair advantage.
senses.example: Several contractors were accused of rigging the bidding process.

synonyms.note: has this meaning in combinations such as fix a match or election
broader and not always dishonest

senses.definition: To equip or arrange something for a particular purpose.
senses.example: The crew rigged the camera with a safety cable before filming.

synonyms.note: more neutral and does not suggest a custom arrangement
broader and often used for complete systems

senses.definition: Equipment or a structure assembled for a particular purpose.
senses.example: The camera operator carried a lightweight shoulder rig.

synonyms.note: broader and less focused on physical equipment

senses.definition: A large truck, especially a tractor-trailer.
senses.example: A big rig pulled into the highway rest area.
senses.usage_note: American English; especially common in the expression big rig.

synonyms.note: more precise and neutral

classification_reason: Widely recognizable slang in entertainment and angry casual speech, but too offensive and person-directed for routine productive use.

senses.definition: An offensive term for a person considered dishonest, cruel, or morally contemptible.
senses.example: The film portrays him as a scumbag who exploits vulnerable people.
senses.usage_note: A strong slang insult; avoid it in professional or neutral descriptions.

synonyms.note: similarly insulting and morally judgmental
milder and usually describes rude or inconsiderate behavior

classification_reason: A common, useful American conversational verb for failing an exam or course, although fail remains the neutral alternative.

senses.definition: To fail an exam, class, or course.
senses.example: I nearly flunked my driving test.
senses.usage_note: Mainly American English and informal; fail is the neutral alternative.

synonyms.note: more neutral and used in a wider range of contexts

antonyms.note: succeed in an exam, class, or course

senses.definition: To give a student a failing grade.
senses.example: The professor flunked two students who had submitted no work.

synonyms.note: more neutral

classification_reason: A common but slangy and sometimes disparaging word with several meanings that are more important to recognize than to produce.

senses.definition: An insulting term for a person considered lazy, dependent on others, or bad at what they do.
senses.example: Angry fans called the referee a bum.
senses.usage_note: Also used disparagingly for an unhoused person; avoid that use.

synonyms.note: the more usual informal American word

senses.definition: To get something from someone by asking for it without paying.
senses.example: Can I bum a ride home from you?
senses.usage_note: Common patterns: bum something off someone and bum something from someone.

senses.definition: Poor in quality, unreliable, or damaged.
senses.example: A bum knee kept her out of the race.

synonyms.note: neutral and much broader
